meaning: Invitar a salir a alguien (en plan romántico)
examples: He finally gathered the courage to ask her out to dinner.
Are you planning to ask him out this weekend?
She asked him out for coffee after the seminar.
I was going to ask her out, but she's already seeing someone.
Don't hesitate to ask someone out if you feel a connection.

meaning: Echarse atrás / Ceder en una discusión o postura
examples: Neither side was willing to back down during the dispute.
He refused to back down despite facing severe public criticism.
She backed down when she realized the evidence against her was solid.
In a heated negotiation, knowing when to back down is a crucial skill.
The company backed down on the proposed wage cuts after the strike.

meaning: Echarse atrás / Retirarse de un acuerdo o compromiso previo
examples: You promised to help us move, so you can't back out now.
The investor backed out of the startup deal at the last minute.
He always backs out whenever a project demands real effort.
She decided to back out of the marathon due to an ankle injury.
It is unprofessional to back out once the contract has been signed.

meaning: Explotar / Estallar en ira / Volverse viral
examples: The bomb squad arrived before the vehicle could blow up.
He blew up at his staff when he noticed the recurring errors.
Her video blew up overnight and gained millions of views.
Try to stay calm and don't blow up over minor inconveniences.
The controversy blew up after an anonymous leak to the press.

meaning: Averiarse / Colapsar emocionalmente / Desglosar en partes
examples: Our car broke down in the middle of the highway.
She broke down in tears when she heard the tragic news.
Let's break down the annual budget into monthly expenditures.
Communication between the two departments completely broke down.
He broke down the complex physics concept into simple terms.

meaning: Entrar a robar / Interrumpir / Estrenar o amoldar ropa/calzado
examples: Burglars attempted to break in while the family was away.
I hate to break in on your conversation, but there is an urgent call.
These leather boots need a few days of walking to break in properly.
The alarm went off as someone tried to break in through the back window.
He gently broke in the new baseball glove before the tournament.

meaning: Romper (una relación/compromiso) / Interrumpir de repente
examples: They decided to break off their engagement after two years.
The prime minister abruptly broke off diplomatic talks.
He broke off in the middle of a sentence when she entered the room.
She broke off a square of chocolate and offered it to me.
The company broke off negotiations with the hostile bidder.

meaning: Estallar (guerra, epidemia, incendio) / Escapar de prisión / Salir sarpullido
examples: Fighting broke out along the disputed border at dawn.
A fire broke out in the hotel kitchen late last night.
Three dangerous inmates managed to break out of the facility.
She breaks out in hives whenever she eats shellfish.
Riots broke out across the capital following the announcement.

meaning: Traspasar una barrera / Lograr un avance decisivo
examples: The sun finally broke through the dense morning fog.
Scientists hope to break through current limitations in battery technology.
The troops managed to break through the enemy defensive lines.
After months of artistic block, she finally broke through with a new novel.
He struggled for years before breaking through in the music industry.

meaning: Separarse / Terminar una relación de pareja / Disolver una multitud
examples: They broke up because they wanted entirely different lifestyles.
The police moved in quickly to break up the unruly protest.
The company will break up its assets into separate independent entities.
You are breaking up; I can't hear you clearly on this phone line.
It took him months to emotionally recover after breaking up with her.

meaning: Causar / Provocar / Dar lugar a un cambio
examples: The new economic policy brought about significant financial growth.
What specific factors brought about this sudden political crisis?
Technological advances have brought about profound changes in education.
His reckless remarks brought about unnecessary tension in the boardroom.
We must collaborate if we want to bring about lasting environmental reform.

meaning: Adelantar (fecha u hora) / Proponer una idea para debate
examples: The committee decided to bring the meeting forward to Tuesday morning.
She brought forward several innovative proposals during the review.
Can we bring forward our appointment by one hour?
The deadline was brought forward due to client pressure.
He brought forward fresh evidence that altered the entire legal case.

meaning: Generar ingresos / Introducir una ley o medida / Incorporar a un experto
examples: His consultancy work brings in substantial extra income.
The government plans to bring in stricter environmental legislation.
We need to bring in an external auditor to evaluate the books.
The summer tourism season brings in millions to local businesses.
They brought in a veteran detective to lead the cold case investigation.

meaning: Llevar a cabo con éxito algo difícil / Lograr una hazaña
examples: Nobody thought they could win the championship, but they brought it off.
It was a daring financial gamble, and she brought it off brilliantly.
He managed to bring off the complex surgical procedure without complications.
Bringing off that diplomatic agreement required months of quiet mediation.
Against all odds, the young director brought off an extraordinary film.

meaning: Provocar la aparición de un síntoma o problema / ¡Que venga! (reto)
examples: Severe fatigue and dehydration can bring on painful muscle spasms.
Stress often brings on his chronic asthma attacks.
I have trained hard all year; bring on the final exam!
Eating excessive sugar may bring on an acute energy crash.
His cold arrogance brought on the hostility of his colleagues.

meaning: Lanzar al mercado un producto / Resaltar o hacer destacar una cualidad
examples: The author is scheduled to bring out her new historical novel in autumn.
Crisis situations tend to bring out the absolute best in dedicated leaders.
That dark blue suit really brings out the vibrant color of your eyes.
The tech giant will bring out its latest smartphone generation next month.
A skilled teacher knows how to bring out the latent potential in quiet students.

meaning: Mencionar un tema / Criar o educar a un menor / Vomitar
examples: Please don't bring up that uncomfortable topic during dinner.
She was brought up in a quiet farming village in northern Spain.
He brought up the budget discrepancy during the annual meeting.
The patient had severe food poisoning and brought up everything he ate.
Raising and bringing up resilient children requires patience and consistency.

meaning: Repasar / Poner al día conocimientos o habilidades oxidadas
examples: I need to brush up on my conversational German before traveling to Berlin.
She spent the weekend brushing up on advanced calculus principles.
He brushed up on corporate law before the job interview.
You should brush up on basic first aid techniques before the camping trip.
It is wise to brush up on local driving regulations before renting a car abroad.

meaning: Cancelar un evento planificado / Ordenar a un animal o persona que se detenga
examples: They had to call off the soccer match due to torrential rain.
The union leaders decided to call off the strike after reaching a settlement.
Call off your guard dog immediately before someone gets hurt!
We were forced to call off the wedding reception after the venue flooded.
Management called off the scheduled merger when hidden debts were found.

meaning: Pedir a alguien formalmente que intervenga / Hacer una visita breve / Apelar a
examples: The president called on all citizens to remain calm and united.
The teacher called on Marcus to answer the historical question.
I plan to call on my elderly aunt on my way back from the clinic.
He called upon his deep reserves of endurance to complete the triathlon.
The charity called on donors to assist families affected by the flood.

meaning: Manejar una situación difícil con éxito / Llevarse un premio
examples: It was a difficult acting role, but she carried it off with remarkable grace.
The young gymnast carried off two gold medals at the national tournament.
He wore an eccentric outfit and managed to carry it off without looking silly.
Carrying off a sensitive negotiation requires emotional intelligence.
Our debate team carried off first prize against tough competitors.

meaning: Continuar / Seguir adelante a pesar de las dificultades
examples: Please carry on with your work; don't let my arrival interrupt you.
She carried on leading the department despite her personal grief.
If you carry on spending recklessly, you will run into severe debt.
The doctor told him he could carry on exercising as long as there was no pain.
We must carry on our ancestors' traditions for future generations.

meaning: Ejecutar / Llevar a la práctica un plan, orden o experimento
examples: Scientists are carrying out extensive clinical trials on the new vaccine.
The military squad carried out the evacuation mission under darkness.
He failed to carry out the specific instructions given by his supervisor.
The hospital carries out hundreds of routine surgeries every week.
We need to carry out a comprehensive security audit of our network.

meaning: Ponerse de moda / Darse cuenta o entender lo que sucede
examples: It took a while, but the innovative software is finally catching on.
He was slow to catch on to the subtle humor of the group.
Do you think electric scooters will really catch on in small towns?
She caught on to their dishonest scheme before losing any money.
The trend caught on among college students almost overnight.

meaning: Alcanzar a alguien / Ponerse al día con tareas, personas o descanso
examples: Walk slower so that the younger children can catch up with us.
Let's meet for lunch tomorrow to catch up on each other's news.
Years of relentless overwork finally caught up with his health.
I need this quiet weekend to catch up on much-needed sleep.
The authorities caught up with the fugitive at the international airport.

meaning: Registrarse en hotel o aeropuerto / Comunicarse brevemente para avisar que estás bien
examples: Passengers are advised to check in at least two hours before departure.
We checked in to the hotel and immediately unpacked our bags.
Just calling to check in and see how your recovery is progressing.
Make sure to check in with the project supervisor before leaving today.
He checked in online to secure an aisle seat on the flight.

meaning: Dejar la habitación de hotel / Pagar en caja / Mirar o examinar algo interesante
examples: Guests must check out of their rooms before eleven in the morning.
You should check out that new bookstore down on Main Street.
The mechanic checked out the engine and confirmed there was no leak.
He waited in line for fifteen minutes to check out at the supermarket.
Check out this fascinating article on artificial intelligence architecture.

meaning: Animar a alguien / Levantarse el ánimo
examples: We brought her fresh flowers to cheer her up after the bad diagnosis.
Cheer up! Things are rarely as hopeless as they initially appear.
Listening to energetic music always helps me cheer up in the morning.
A thoughtful phone call from an old friend can really cheer someone up.
He tried cracking jokes to cheer up his anxious teammates before the game.

meaning: Despejarse (el clima) / Curarse una infección / Aclarar un malentendido
examples: The dark clouds drifted away and the sky cleared up by noon.
I hope this antibiotic ointment will clear up the rash within days.
We need to clear up this scheduling misunderstanding right away.
Please clear up your desk before heading home for the weekend.
Once the confusion cleared up, the project proceeded smoothly.

meaning: Toparse con alguien/algo por casualidad / Dar una impresión o parecer de cierta forma
examples: I came across an ancient Roman coin while digging in the backyard.
She comes across as extremely confident and articulate in interviews.
Have you ever come across such an unusual linguistic structure?
He came across as aloof, but he was simply painfully shy.
I came across your father's old letters while cleaning out the attic.

meaning: Acompañar a alguien / Progresar / Aparecer una oportunidad
examples: We are going for a hike in the hills; do you want to come along?
How is your master's research paper coming along these days?
Grab this career opportunity if it comes along; don't wait.
Medical treatments for this condition have come along remarkably fast.
He invited his brother to come along on the fishing excursion.

meaning: Pasar de visita brevemente / Conseguir algo difícil de obtener
examples: Feel free to come by my office whenever you have technical questions.
Authentic handmade leather goods are difficult to come by nowadays.
How did you come by such rare first-edition philosophical volumes?
She came by the apartment yesterday evening to drop off the house keys.
Honest, reliable business partners are getting harder to come by.

meaning: Reducirse esencialmente a / Depender en última instancia de
examples: In professional athletics, success often comes down to mental resilience.
The legal dispute finally came down to the interpretation of one single clause.
When you analyze human motivation, much of it comes down to security and dignity.
It all comes down to whether you are willing to make the necessary sacrifices.
The championship came down to the final penalty kick of the match.

meaning: Presentarse voluntariamente para declarar o prestar ayuda
examples: Police urged any potential witnesses to come forward with information.
Several former employees came forward to testify against corporate fraud.
No one came forward to claim the abandoned suitcase found at the station.
Volunteers came forward immediately to assist with emergency flood relief.
She had the moral courage to come forward and report the harassment.

meaning: Salir al mercado / Publicarse / Revelarse la verdad / Salir el sol
examples: His new historical documentary is scheduled to come out next month.
The truth will inevitably come out sooner or later.
After hours of freezing rain, the afternoon sun finally came out.
How did the final architectural calculations come out after review?
She decided to come out to her family regarding her true identity.

meaning: Recuperar el conocimiento / Cambiar de opinión / Pasar de visita
examples: The boxer was knocked out cold but came round after a minute.
He was strictly opposed at first, but he will come round to our idea.
Why don't you come round for dinner on Friday evening?
She fainted from dehydration and came round in the emergency ward.
Give him time; he usually comes round once he analyzes the facts calmly.

meaning: Idear / Ocurrirse una idea, plan, dinero o solución
examples: Our creative marketing squad needs to come up with an engaging campaign.
He managed to come up with the emergency bail money within three hours.
Can anyone come up with a realistic solution to this logistics bottleneck?
She came up with a brilliant thesis proposal that impressed the faculty.
We must come up with an alternative route to avoid city center traffic.

meaning: Contar con alguien / Confiar en que algo ocurrirá
examples: You can always count on David to deliver accurate financial reports.
Do not count on good weather for an outdoor wedding in November.
She is someone I can count on through every existential crisis.
We were counting on their foreign investment to expand operations.
Never count on luck when proper preparation can guarantee success.

meaning: Reducir el consumo o gasto de algo
examples: The doctor advised him to cut back on sodium and processed carbohydrates.
During the recession, households cut back on non-essential entertainment.
We need to cut back on operational expenses without firing employees.
She is trying to cut back on screen time before going to sleep.
The municipal council cut back on street lighting to save energy.

meaning: Disminuir la cantidad de algo que se ingiere o hace
examples: I am trying to cut down on caffeine to improve my sleep quality.
He cut down on smoking from a pack a day to just two cigarettes.
We should cut down on plastic packaging whenever possible.
Cutting down on refined sugar had an immediate positive impact on her energy.
The company is striving to cut down on unnecessary international travel.

meaning: Cortar el suministro / Aislar geográficamente / Interrumpir a alguien
examples: The heavy snowstorm cut off several remote mountain hamlets.
The utility company cut off our water supply due to an administrative error.
Don't cut me off while I am presenting my technical argument.
The reckless driver cut us off abruptly on the interstate highway.
His wealthy family threatened to cut him off if he dropped out of law school.

meaning: Eliminar de la dieta o rutina / Dejar de funcionar súbitamente / ¡Para ya!
examples: The cardiologist told him to cut out saturated trans fats completely.
The boat engine suddenly cut out while we were ten miles offshore.
Cut it out! You are driving everyone crazy with that repetitive tapping.
She cut out toxic online forums to preserve her mental health.
He is not cut out for the high-stress environment of emergency surgery.

meaning: Lidiar con / Gestionar un problema o persona / Tratar sobre un tema
examples: A seasoned manager knows how to deal with customer grievances calmly.
This theoretical book deals with the philosophical foundations of ethics.
I simply don't have the emotional energy to deal with his complaints today.
We must deal with the water leak before it damages the hardwood floors.
He had to deal with intense bereavement following the unexpected loss.

meaning: Abolir / Deshacerse de / Suprimir una norma, ley o costumbre
examples: The government decided to do away with outdated agricultural tariffs.
Many modern offices want to do away with rigid nine-to-five schedules.
It is time to do away with redundant bureaucratic paperwork in hospitals.
The progressive school did away with traditional standardized grading.
Some radical theorists argue we should do away with physical cash entirely.

meaning: Pasar sin algo / Prescindir de algo necesario
examples: We ran out of milk, so you will have to do without it in your coffee today.
In times of scarcity, our grandparents learned to do without luxuries.
I could really do without his cynical commentary during our staff meetings.
No human organism can do without clean drinking water for more than a few days.
We will have to do without a vacation abroad this year to pay for renovations.

meaning: Redactar un documento formal / Detenerse un vehículo junto a algo
examples: Our corporate attorneys are drawing up the final merger agreement.
A sleek black limousine drew up right outside the embassy gates.
Take time to draw up a clear outline before writing your master's thesis.
The military commander drew up a detailed tactical retreat plan.
She drew up a list of pros and cons before accepting the international job.

meaning: Pasar de visita informalmente y sin cita previa
examples: Please drop by anytime you are passing through our neighborhood.
My neighbor dropped in unexpectedly to borrow some garden tools.
I'll drop by the dry cleaner on my way back from the office.
Feel free to drop in on our laboratory seminar tomorrow morning.
He dropped by his parents' house to check how their heating was working.

meaning: Dejar a alguien/algo de camino / Quedarse dormido sin querer / Disminuir
examples: Can you drop me off at the train station on your commute to work?
He was so exhausted that he dropped off during the keynote speech.
Tourism bookings dropped off sharply after the hurricane warning.
I need to drop off this legal parcel at the post office before five.
Sales numbers dropped off in the fourth quarter due to supply delays.

meaning: Abandonar los estudios / Retirarse de una competición o sociedad
examples: Steve Jobs famously dropped out of college after one semester.
He had to drop out of the cycling marathon because of heat exhaustion.
Many talented students drop out due to severe financial pressure.
She chose to drop out of the corporate rat race and open a ceramic studio.
The runner dropped out at the twenty-mile mark with torn knee ligaments.

meaning: Aflojar / Calmarse / Disminuir de intensidad (lluvia, dolor, presión)
examples: The pouring rain began to ease off as the storm system moved east.
The doctor promised the acute pain would ease off within forty-eight hours.
The manager should ease off on the criticism before he demoralizes the staff.
Once traffic eased off after rush hour, we reached the airport quickly.
He decided to ease off on his training intensity to prevent muscle tearing.

meaning: Acabar / Ir a parar a un lugar, situación o estado inesperado
examples: We took a wrong turn and ended up in a deserted industrial district.
If you continue gambling recklessly, you will end up bankrupt.
She studied civil engineering but ended up working as an animator.
He ended up spending three years in prison for financial embezzlement.
How did we end up arguing about something so completely trivial?

meaning: Afrontar con valentía una verdad o situación difícil
examples: You must face up to the reality that this business model is unviable.
He refused to face up to his growing alcohol dependency for years.
It is painful to face up to the fact that someone you loved deceived you.
Leaders must face up to their errors rather than scapegoating subordinates.
She finally faced up to her chronic anxiety and sought clinical support.

meaning: Desmoronarse físicamente o emocionalmente / Fracasar un acuerdo
examples: This antique leather sofa is starting to fall apart at the seams.
Her emotional composure fell apart when she heard the verdict.
The peace treaty fell apart within days of being drafted.
Without disciplined leadership, the volunteer organization fell apart.
He felt like his entire world was falling apart after the sudden divorce.

meaning: Quedarse rezagado / Retrasarse en pagos o tareas
examples: He was sick for two weeks and fell behind in his university coursework.
Do not fall behind on your mortgage payments, or interest will compound.
Our company fell behind competitors because we hesitated to digitize.
The exhausted hiker fell behind the main group on the mountain ascent.
She worked overtime on weekends to avoid falling behind on project goals.

meaning: Enamorarse locamente de alguien / Tragarse un engaño o timo
examples: He fell for her charm the very first moment they spoke at the gallery.
I can't believe you fell for that obvious phishing email scam.
She always falls for charismatic people who turn out to be unreliable.
Don't fall for slick marketing slogans; inspect the technical specifications.
He fell for the fake investment pitch and lost his life savings.

meaning: Discutir y distanciarse de alguien / Caerse (dientes, pelo)
examples: The two lifelong business partners fell out over money allocations.
Her hair began to fall out during the intensive chemotherapy treatment.
They fell out five years ago and haven't spoken a single word since.
I hate falling out with family members over petty political disputes.
Baby teeth naturally fall out to make way for permanent dentition.

meaning: Venirse abajo / Fracasar un plan, acuerdo o venta
examples: The real estate deal fell through when the buyer failed to secure a mortgage.
Our holiday travel plans fell through due to sudden flight cancellations.
If the funding falls through, we will have to suspend archaeological excavations.
All our logistical preparations fell through at the eleventh hour.
He was deeply disappointed when the promising job offer fell through.

meaning: Descifrar / Comprender / Resolver algo tras reflexionar
examples: I cannot figure out why this computer algorithm throws a runtime error.
It took her months to figure out what career path truly fulfilled her.
Can you figure out how to assemble this flat-pack wardrobe?
Detectives worked round the clock to figure out the burglar's motive.
We need to figure out a viable exit strategy before signing the lease.

meaning: Rellenar un formulario / Poner al tanto a alguien / Sustituir a un compañero
examples: Please fill out this registration form with your passport details.
Can you fill me in on what was discussed during the morning briefing?
She agreed to fill in for her sick colleague during the night shift.
Make sure you fill in every required section before submitting the grant.
He filled his supervisor in on the unexpected client negotiations.

meaning: Descubrir / Enterarse de una información o verdad
examples: She was devastated when she found out that her partner had lied.
I need to find out what time the last express train departs for Madrid.
How did you find out about this confidential investment opportunity?
If the press finds out about this financial cover-up, the minister will resign.
We ran rigorous laboratory tests to find out the precise cause of contamination.

meaning: Encajar socialmente / Encontrar hueco en la agenda para algo
examples: It was difficult for the immigrant child to fit in at the new school initially.
The doctor can fit you in for a brief consultation at four this afternoon.
He altered his personal style in a desperate attempt to fit in with the group.
Does this modern glass building really fit in with the historic architecture?
I'll try to fit in a gym session between my afternoon client meetings.

meaning: Hacerse entender / Transmitir una idea con claridad
examples: The speaker struggled to get his message across to the hostile crowd.
Use concrete real-world metaphors to get complex scientific theories across.
Did I manage to get across the urgency of meeting this regulatory deadline?
She used evocative sketches to get her architectural vision across.
Body language plays an enormous role in getting your true intentions across.

meaning: Progresar / Prosperar profesional o financieramente
examples: In modern industry, continuous self-education is essential to get ahead.
He worked sixty hours a week because he was determined to get ahead.
Ethical compromises may help you get ahead temporarily, but they ruin reputations.
Saving a portion of every paycheck allows families to get ahead financially.
She utilized her bilingual fluency to get ahead in the diplomatic corps.

meaning: Llevarse bien con alguien / Entenderse
examples: Do you get along well with your direct supervisor and teammates?
The two brothers never got along during childhood, but are close now.
It is impossible to build high-performing teams if members can't get along.
She gets along with almost everyone thanks to her empathetic disposition.
How are you getting along with your new flatmates in Barcelona?

meaning: Insinuar / Llegar a alcanzar algo físico / Descubrir la verdad
examples: What exactly are you getting at with those veiled accusations?
Store household cleaning chemicals on high shelves where toddlers cannot get at them.
The investigative committee is working tirelessly to get at the truth.
I couldn't quite understand what the philosophical essay was getting at.
Stop beating around the bush and tell me what you are getting at.

meaning: Salir impune de algo malo / Salirse con la suya
examples: He thought he could commit corporate tax fraud and get away with it.
Don't let your spoiled children get away with disrespectful behavior.
She broke the company safety rules and somehow got away with a warning.
A seasoned corrupt official rarely gets away with embezzlement indefinitely.
You cannot get away with plagiarism in a serious academic institution.

meaning: Apañárselas / Salir adelante con lo justo (dinero, idioma)
examples: My spoken French is basic, but it is enough to get by as a tourist.
After losing his primary job, he had to get by on his modest savings.
Many low-income families struggle to get by as inflation rises.
We don't need excessive luxury; we can easily get by with essentials.
She got by on four hours of sleep a night during final exam week.

meaning: Ponerse en serio con una tarea / Ir al grano
examples: Enough small talk; let's get down to business and review the budget.
It is time to stop procrastinating and get down to writing the report.
She shut off her smartphone to get down to serious dissertation research.
We need to get down to the root cause of this mechanical failure.
Once everyone arrived, the committee got down to drafting the bylaws.

meaning: Superar una enfermedad, pérdida, ruptura o impresión
examples: It took her two full weeks to get over that severe strain of influenza.
He has never truly gotten over the heartbreak of that broken engagement.
I still can't get over how magnificent the Andean mountain views were.
You need to get over your fear of public speaking to advance your career.
Give yourself time to mourn; you don't have to get over a tragedy overnight.

meaning: Deshacerse de algo o alguien molesto / Eliminar
examples: We spent the whole Saturday getting rid of old furniture and clothes.
How can I get rid of this persistent headache without prescription pills?
The corporate board voted to get rid of the underperforming executive.
It is healthy to get rid of toxic habits that drain your vital energy.
The city council launched an initiative to get rid of abandoned vehicles.

meaning: Encontrar por fin el tiempo para hacer algo pendiente
examples: I have been meaning to paint the kitchen, but I haven't got round to it.
Did you ever get around to reading that existential philosophy book?
She finally got round to replying to all her overdue client emails.
I will fix the squeaking door hinge as soon as I get around to it.
He never got around to renewing his passport before the trip was booked.

meaning: Superar un periodo duro / Comunicar por teléfono / Hacer entender a alguien
examples: With the loyalty of good friends, you can get through any tragedy.
I tried calling the customer support hotline for hours, but couldn't get through.
I have tried reasoning with him, but I simply cannot get through to him.
She got through the grueling four-year medical residency successfully.
A teacher must find creative approaches to get through to disengaged pupils.

meaning: Regalar / Donar / Revelar un secreto o final de una historia
examples: They decided to give away all their duplicate household goods to charity.
Don't give away the ending of the mystery movie; I haven't watched it yet!
His trembling hands gave away his intense nervous anxiety.
The store is giving away free promotional samples to the first fifty buyers.
Her subtle smile gave away the fact that she already knew the surprise.

meaning: Ceder ante la presión o insistencia / Darse por vencido
examples: After hours of persistent whining, the weary father gave in and bought the toy.
Never give in to tyrannical bullies; stand your ground with dignity.
The municipal government finally gave in to public environmental demands.
He fought the disease with remarkable fortitude, refusing to give in.
The military garrison surrendered only when ammunition ran out completely.

meaning: Rendirse / Abandonar un hábito o vicio
examples: He gave up smoking after his cardiologist warned him of arterial blockages.
Never give up on your noble aspirations, no matter how steep the incline.
I give up! What is the answer to this impossible mathematical riddle?
She gave up her lucrative corporate career to work for humanitarian causes.
Don't give up when you are only a few steps away from your destination.

meaning: Proceder / Llevar a cabo una acción / Dar permiso
examples: The board gave us the green light to go ahead with the factory expansion.
Go ahead, eat your dinner; don't wait for me to finish my call.
Despite fierce criticism, the mayor went ahead with the urban zoning plan.
Can we go ahead and finalize the contract with the international supplier?
If you truly believe in your artistic project, go ahead and pursue it.

meaning: Aceptar o secundar una propuesta, plan o norma
examples: I am willing to go along with your proposed strategy for this quarter.
He refused to go along with fraudulent corporate accounting practices.
She reluctantly went along with her friends' plan to visit the crowded club.
It is easier to go along with the crowd, but moral progress requires dissent.
The senate agreed to go along with the president's emergency fiscal package.

meaning: Romper o faltar a una promesa, palabra o juramento
examples: An honorable leader never goes back on his sworn word.

She felt betrayed when her closest confidant went back on their agreement.
Do not make promises lightly if there is any chance you might go back on them.
Going back on your legal obligations carries severe financial liability.

meaning: Explotar (bomba) / Sonar (alarma) / Estropearse comida / Perder el interés
examples: My alarm clock went off at five in the morning, waking the entire house.
A firecracker went off right outside the window, startling the dog.
Smell this milk before drinking; I think it has gone off in the heat.
She went off on her assistant in an unprofessional fit of temper.
He used to love horror video games, but he has completely gone off them lately.

meaning: Continuar / Suceder o pasar / Seguir hablando sin parar
examples: What on earth is going on here? Why is there water on the living room floor?
Please go on with your explanation; I am listening with acute attention.
Life must go on, even after enduring unimaginable personal grief.
He can go on for hours about sixteenth-century naval architecture.
The street festival went on late into the night despite the cold drizzle.

meaning: Revisar detalladamente / Repasar un texto o plan / Ser recibido por el público
examples: Let's go over the commercial contract once more before signing.
She spent two hours going over her lecture notes before the final exam.
The director went over the scene with the actors before shooting.
His controversial joke did not go over well with the corporate audience.
Always go over your tax return calculations to prevent costly errors.

meaning: Atravesar una etapa dura / Examinar a fondo / Aprobarse una ley
examples: She went through an agonizing divorce while launching her own business.
Customs officers went through every single piece of our checked luggage.
The proposed tax legislation finally went through after marathon debates.
We had to go through dozens of scientific journals to find the cited data.
He is going through a severe existential crisis regarding his life aim.

meaning: Distanciarse emocionalmente con el tiempo (amistad, pareja)
examples: They were inseparable in high school, but gradually grew apart at university.
It is painful when married partners grow apart after the children leave home.
Having different moral values often causes close friends to grow apart.
We didn't fight or argue; our life trajectories simply caused us to grow apart.
Don't let busy work schedules cause you and your partner to grow apart.

meaning: Quedarle pequeña la ropa / Superar con la edad un hábito o miedo infantil
examples: Children grow out of their winter shoes at an astonishingly rapid pace.
Most toddlers eventually grow out of throwing public tantrums.
He never grew out of his childhood passion for astronomy and physics.
She grew out of her fear of dark basements as she reached adolescence.
This ambitious startup grew out of a modest student research project.

meaning: Pasar el rato / Relajarse con amigos / Tender la ropa
examples: Teenagers often hang out at the shopping mall on Saturday afternoons.
Where do you and your university colleagues usually hang out after lectures?
She hung out the wet laundry in the garden to dry in the summer breeze.
I enjoy hanging out with friends who stimulate my intellectual curiosity.
Let's hang out this weekend and listen to some classic vinyl records.

meaning: Contener lágrimas, emociones o golpes / Frenar el avance o progreso
examples: She struggled to hold back her tears during her father's eulogy.
Fear of failure is the single greatest obstacle holding young artists back.
He held back his anger and replied with measured professional courtesy.
The concrete retaining wall held back the torrential mudslide.
Do not hold back during the audition; showcase your absolute vocal power.

meaning: Esperar un momento / Agarrarse fuerte / Resistir en una dificultad
examples: Hold on for a second; let me grab a pen to write down your address.
Hold on tight to the boat railing; the ocean waves are getting choppy.
If you can just hold on for two more months, financial relief is coming.
The besieged soldiers held on against overwhelming odds until reinforcements arrived.
Hold on! Are you telling me that the entire database was accidentally deleted?

meaning: Demorar / Sostener físicamente / Resistir el paso del tiempo / Atracar
examples: Heavy highway construction held us up for more than forty minutes.
Four thick marble columns hold up the roof of the ancient cathedral.
How is your grandmother holding up after the surgical operation?
His theoretical argument does not hold up under rigorous empirical scrutiny.
Masked bandits attempted to hold up the local post office at gunpoint.

meaning: Continuar haciendo algo / No dejar de insistir
examples: Keep on practicing every single day, and your accent will improve markedly.
Despite repeated discouragement, she kept on applying for research grants.
Why do you keep on interrupting me when I am trying to explain the issue?
He kept on running even after severe blisters formed on both feet.
Keep on walking up the hill; the mountain shelter is just around the bend.

meaning: Mantener el ritmo de alguien / Mantenerse al día con noticias o novedades
examples: Walk a bit slower; the elderly tourists can't keep up with your pace.
It is demanding to keep up with the rapid developments in artificial intelligence.
Keep up the excellent academic work, and you will graduate with honors.
He tried to keep up appearances despite facing catastrophic bankruptcy.
She reads international journals daily to keep up with economic trends.

meaning: Despedir trabajadores por recorte / Dejar en paz / Dejar de consumir
examples: The automotive manufacturer had to lay off five hundred assembly workers.
Lay off him! Can't you see he is already stressed and exhausted?
The doctor told him to lay off heavy lifting until his lumbar hernia healed.
During economic downturns, tech firms frequently lay off administrative staff.
Lay off the sugary snacks if you want to maintain balanced insulin levels.

meaning: Decepcionar a alguien que confiaba en ti / Desinflar / Alargar ropa
examples: I promised to help my brother, and I cannot let him down now.
The final episode of that acclaimed mystery series let many viewers down.
She felt deeply let down when her business mentor broke his promise.
A dependable friend will never let you down in times of existential trial.
The seamstress let down the hem of the trousers by two inches.

meaning: Cuidar de una persona, animal, casa o asunto
examples: Could you please look after our golden retriever while we are on vacation?
She spent five years looking after her ailing grandmother with devotion.
Make sure you look after your physical health while studying for finals.
A conscientious tenant looks after the rented apartment as if it were his own.
Who is going to look after the shop while the manager is at the trade fair?

meaning: Mirar por encima del hombro / Menospreciar con arrogancia
examples: Never look down on someone simply because they work in manual trades.
He looked down on anyone who didn't possess an Ivy League academic degree.
Her aristocratic relatives always looked down on her modest lifestyle.
It is a sign of deep insecurity when people look down on others to feel superior.
The arrogant critic looked down on mainstream cinematic blockbusters.

meaning: Esperar con ilusión o ganas un evento futuro (+ ing/sustantivo)
examples: I am genuinely looking forward to meeting your family in Seville.
She looks forward to unwinding with a book after a demanding work week.
We always look forward to celebrating the winter solstice together.
Looking forward to hearing from you at your earliest convenience.
The children are looking forward to visiting the marine aquarium on Friday.

meaning: Investigar / Examinar a fondo un asunto o queja
examples: The police department promised to look into the neighborhood burglaries.
We are looking into the feasibility of installing solar panels on the roof.
Our compliance committee will look into the allegations of financial fraud.
Have you looked into the tuition costs for that international master's degree?
The engineering team is looking into the cause of yesterday's system blackout.

meaning: Tener cuidado / Prestar atención para no tropezar o ser engañado
examples: Look out! There is a patch of black ice right on the driveway.
Always look out for pickpockets when traveling on crowded subway cars.
Good team captains always look out for the welfare of their younger players.
Look out for hidden clauses and unexpected penalties in commercial contracts.
He told his younger sister to look out for herself while living in the metropolis.

meaning: Buscar información en diccionario/internet / Mejorar la situación
examples: If you don't know the definition of a word, look it up in the dictionary.
After months of severe financial hardship, things are finally looking up.
I'll look up the airline flight schedule and confirm our departure terminal.
Sales numbers were dismal in spring, but the economic outlook is looking up.
Look up his contact phone number on the official university directory.

meaning: Admirar y respetar profundamente a alguien como modelo a seguir
examples: Young athletes all over the world look up to her dedication and sportsmanship.
He has always looked up to his elder brother as a paragon of integrity.
Children naturally look up to parents who embody truthfulness and courage.
She is the kind of thoughtful mentor that junior researchers truly look up to.
Who did you look up to the most while you were navigating adolescence?

meaning: Distinguir con dificultad / Entender / Besarse apasionadamente / Fingir
examples: I could barely make out the distant lighthouse through the dense fog.
His handwritten signature was so messy that nobody could make it out.
The teenagers were making out on the back bench of the cinema.
She made out that she was an experienced executive, but it was all an act.
Can you make out what the speaker on the radio is trying to say?

meaning: Inventar (historia, excusa) / Reconciliarse tras una pelea / Maquillarse
examples: He made up a ridiculous excuse for arriving two hours late to the board meeting.
The couple had a fierce argument yesterday, but they made up this morning.
She spent twenty minutes making herself up before the formal gala dinner.
Women make up more than half of the current medical school student body.
Don't just make up data points; verify your statistics against reliable registries.

meaning: Compensar por una falta, error o tiempo perdido
examples: He worked double shifts on the weekend to make up for lost time.
No amount of financial compensation can make up for the loss of a loved one.
She bought him a thoughtful gift to make up for forgetting his anniversary.
His extraordinary stamina makes up for his slight lack of raw technical speed.
We organized an extra seminar to make up for the cancelled lecture.

meaning: Fallecer / Morir (eufemismo respetuoso)
examples: Her beloved grandfather passed away peacefully in his sleep at ninety-two.
We were deeply saddened to hear that our former literature professor had passed away.
After battling illness for years, the acclaimed author passed away yesterday.
He passed away surrounded by his devoted children and grandchildren.
The family requested privacy after the prominent statesman passed away.

meaning: Desmayarse / Perder el conocimiento / Repartir hojas o folletos
examples: The hall was so hot and stuffy that two audience members passed out.
He passed out from dehydration after running twenty miles under the midday sun.
The teacher asked Marcus to pass out the exam papers to the class.
She felt dizzy, sat down on the bench, and promptly passed out.
Volunteers passed out warm blankets and hot tea to the homeless refugees.

meaning: Devolver dinero prestado / Vengarse de alguien por un agravio
examples: I will pay you back every cent as soon as I receive my monthly paycheck.
He swore he would pay back the rivals who had betrayed his trust.
Make sure to pay back your bank loans on time to preserve your credit rating.
She paid back her parents for supporting her through medical school.
Forgiveness is morally superior to spending your life plotting to pay someone back.

meaning: Elegir entre varias opciones / Reconocer o distinguir entre una multitud
examples: Take your time and pick out the necktie that best matches your wedding suit.
The witness was able to pick out the burglar from the police lineup immediately.
She picked out three antique ceramic plates at the flea market.
It was impossible to pick out his voice amidst the roaring stadium crowd.
The committee picked out the most promising candidates for round two.

meaning: Recoger del suelo o en coche / Aprender sin esfuerzo / Contestar el teléfono / Mejorar
examples: Can you pick up the children from their primary school this afternoon?
She lived in Rome for six months and picked up conversational Italian easily.
I called his personal mobile four times, but he refused to pick up.
Economic activity in the industrial sector is finally beginning to pick up.
Please pick up your toys from the living room rug before going to bed.

meaning: Señalar con el dedo / Indicar o hacer notar un hecho o error
examples: The tour guide pointed out the historic cathedral's Gothic bell tower.
She was quick to point out several mathematical discrepancies in his ledger.
I must point out that our operating budget has already exceeded its ceiling.
He pointed out that correlation does not necessarily imply direct causation.
Thank you for pointing out that typographical error before we printed the books.

meaning: Dejar en el suelo / Menospreciar o humillar / Sacrificar a un animal enfermo
examples: Put down that heavy cardboard box before you hurt your lumbar back.
A cruel manager continually puts down his subordinates to feel powerful.
The veterinarian gently explained that it was time to put our elderly dog down.
Put down your mobile phones and pay attention to the seminar speaker.
She put down a ten-percent financial deposit on the new downtown apartment.

meaning: Posponer / Desanimar o dar repelús / Desconcertar
examples: Never put off until tomorrow what you can accomplish with discipline today.
The board meeting was put off until Friday due to the president's illness.
The unpleasant odor coming from the kitchen put me off eating entirely.
His arrogant and aggressive tone really put off potential business investors.
Don't be put off by initial difficulties; language mastery requires patience.

meaning: Ponerse ropa/calzado / Subir de peso / Montar un espectáculo / Fingir
examples: Put on your warm woolen coat; the temperature has dropped below freezing.
He put on ten kilograms of lean muscle after a year of weightlifting.
The local drama society is putting on a production of Hamlet this winter.
She is not truly grieving; she is just putting on a dramatic act for sympathy.
Can you put on some soothing classical music while we prepare dinner?

meaning: Extinguir un fuego o cigarro / Publicar / Molestar o causar un inconveniente
examples: Firefighters worked for five hours to put out the raging chemical blaze.
Please put out your cigarette before entering the hospital courtyard.
The university press will put out the revised historical monograph in May.
I hope I'm not putting you out by asking to stay on your sofa tonight.
The municipal council put out an urgent public warning regarding floodwaters.

meaning: Tolerar / Aguantar una situación o persona desagradable
examples: I refuse to put up with his continuous insolence and chronic tardiness.
How do you put up with the deafening traffic noise outside your apartment?
She has put up with difficult working conditions for years without complaining.
A healthy relationship cannot survive if one partner has to put up with deceit.
Tenants should not have to put up with a leaking roof and broken heating.

meaning: Confiar en / Depender de algo o alguien para funcionar
examples: Modern society relies heavily on uninterrupted electrical power grids.
You can always rely on Maria to keep confidential business matters secret.
Do not rely solely on automated spellcheckers when writing formal contracts.
The elderly couple relies on their eldest daughter for grocery shopping.
He relied on his deep faith and family support to endure the tragedy.

meaning: Descartar una hipótesis, sospechoso, opción o posibilidad
examples: Physicians ran an MRI scan to rule out any acute cerebral injury.
We cannot rule out the possibility of an early election this autumn.
The detective ruled out the night watchman as a potential robbery suspect.
Heavy financial costs ruled out an immediate expansion into Asian markets.
Never rule out a candidate before conducting a thorough personal interview.

meaning: Tropezar por casualidad con alguien / Chocar contra / Encontrarse con problemas
examples: Guess who I ran into while shopping at the supermarket yesterday?
The delivery van skidded on the wet ice and ran into a concrete lamppost.
We ran into unexpected legal obstacles while registering our company trademark.
If you undertake complex renovations, you will inevitably run into delays.
I ran into an old university professor at the international conference.

meaning: Quedarse sin existencias de algo (tiempo, dinero, combustible)
examples: We must pull into the nearest gas station; we are running out of fuel.
Hurry up and conclude your presentation; we are quickly running out of time.
The hospital nearly ran out of oxygen tanks during the winter epidemic.
He ran out of excuses when presented with the security camera footage.
I wanted to bake a cake, but I realized I had completely run out of eggs.

meaning: Partir de viaje / Activar una alarma / Provocar una cadena de eventos
examples: We set off on our cross-country road trip at five in the morning.
Burnt toast in the cafeteria kitchen set off the building's fire alarms.
The unexpected assassination set off a catastrophic continental war.
Her tactless remark set off an uncomfortable argument around the dinner table.
Hikers packed lightweight gear and set off towards the mountain summit.

meaning: Montar / Fundar una empresa / Tender una trampa / Configurar un equipo
examples: She decided to leave her corporate job and set up her own legal firm.
Can you help me set up the audiovisual projector in the conference room?
The criminal claimed he was innocent and that corrupt rivals had set him up.
They set up a charitable foundation to fund research into childhood leukemia.
It took thirty minutes to set up the outdoor camping tent in the dark.

meaning: Presumir / Alardear de habilidades o posesiones
examples: He loves driving with his car windows down just to show off his luxury vehicle.
She was not trying to show off; she was simply answering the examiner's question.
Stop showing off in front of your friends; modesty is far more attractive.
The acrobat showed off his astonishing balance on the high wire.
He bought that exorbitant watch purely to show off his newfound wealth.

meaning: Aparecer / Presentarse en un lugar / Dejar en evidencia a alguien
examples: We waited for forty minutes, but he didn't show up for the interview.
Hundreds of enthusiastic citizens showed up for the charity marathon.
Her brilliant scientific presentation completely showed up the keynote speaker.
It is rude to show up at someone's residence unannounced at dinner time.
The missing courier finally showed up with the confidential documents.

meaning: Significar (siglas) / Tolerar o permitir / Defender principios
examples: What do the letters 'UNESCO' actually stand for in international law?
I will not stand for such insolent and insubordinate conduct in my classroom.
Our political party stands for individual liberty and economic fairness.
A soldier must know precisely what principles his uniform stands for.
The abbreviation 'e.g.' stands for the Latin phrase 'exempli gratia'.

meaning: Destacar visiblemente / Sobresalir por calidad o diferencia
examples: Her bright yellow raincoat made her stand out distinctly in the crowded plaza.
His exceptional analytical abilities made him stand out among applicants.
To get hired in a competitive field, your CV needs to stand out from the stack.
One unexpected historical detail stood out during our archival research.
True leaders stand out by maintaining composure when everyone else panics.

meaning: Parecerse a un familiar (en rasgos físicos o de carácter)
examples: She takes after her mother in both her musical talent and stubbornness.
Marcus takes after his paternal grandfather with his tall, lean build.
He has a hot temper; he clearly takes after his father in that regard.
Do your children take after you or your spouse in personality?
The young painter takes after her artistic uncle in her eye for vibrant color.

meaning: Asimilar información / Acoger en casa / Engañar / Meter la ropa
examples: The lecture was so dense that I could barely take in all the theory.
The charitable couple took in three stray animals during the winter freeze.
Don't be taken in by smooth-talking salespeople offering easy riches.
After losing weight, she had to take in the waistline of all her skirts.
He sat in stunned silence, trying to take in the tragic news he had received.

meaning: Despegar (avión) / Despegar con éxito (negocio) / Quitarse ropa / Marcharse
examples: The commercial airliner took off smoothly despite the gusty headwinds.
Her online artisanal bakery business really took off during the pandemic.
Please take off your muddy boots before walking on the polished hardwood.
He took off his glasses and rubbed his exhausted eyes before answering.
I'm sorry, but I have an urgent appointment; I have to take off right now.

meaning: Hacerse cargo del control / Tomar el relevo o asumir una empresa
examples: The multinational conglomerate plans to take over its smaller domestic rival.
I am feeling dizzy; can you take over the steering wheel for an hour?
Artificial intelligence is unlikely to take over all creative professions soon.
When the general died, his most capable lieutenant took over command.
Don't let unexamined bitterness take over your entire philosophical outlook.

meaning: Cogerle gusto o cariño a algo/alguien / Adquirir un hábito nuevo
examples: The rescue dog took to its new adoptive family almost immediately.
He took to oil painting like a natural from his very first art lesson.
She has taken to walking five miles every morning before sunrise.
The young students took to the charismatic substitute teacher right away.
He took to drinking heavy spirits to drown his mounting anxiety.

meaning: Empezar una afición o deporte / Ocupar espacio o tiempo / Acortar una prenda
examples: He decided to take up Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu to improve his physical conditioning.
That massive antique bookcase takes up far too much room in our small parlor.
Writing a doctoral thesis will take up virtually all your weekend leisure time.
She took up the trousers by two centimeters so they wouldn't drag on the floor.
He took up the company's generous relocation offer without hesitation.

meaning: Echar una bronca / Regañar a alguien con severidad por su mala conducta
examples: The librarian told off the teenagers for shouting and throwing books.
Her mother told her off for leaving dirty dishes piled in the sink.
He finally told off his arrogant colleague after months of subtle disrespect.
The referee told off the aggressive defender for a reckless sliding tackle.
She was terrified her supervisor would tell her off for arriving forty minutes late.

meaning: Meditar / Reflexionar cuidadosamente antes de tomar una decisión
examples: Take the weekend to think over our job offer before making your decision.
He promised to think over her proposal and provide an answer by Tuesday.
Don't resign impulsively; think things over when your emotions have calmed.
She sat by the seashore, thinking over the major crossroads in her life.
It is wise to think over the long-term ethical implications of this venture.

meaning: Tirar a la basura / Desperdiciar una oportunidad de oro
examples: Don't throw away those cardboard boxes; we can reuse them for storage.
He threw away a brilliant academic career because of his gambling addiction.
She threw out all the expired pharmaceutical medicines from the cabinet.
Throwing away an opportunity to study abroad is something you may regret.
Please throw your trash into the municipal recycling bin on the corner.

meaning: Rechazar una oferta o solicitud / Bajar el volumen o intensidad
examples: She turned down the prestigious scholarship because it required relocating.
Could you please turn down the television? I am trying to read this contract.
He felt humiliated after the bank turned down his small business loan request.
Never turn down constructive professional mentorship out of wounded vanity.
Turn down the stove heat to a gentle simmer once the broth boils.

meaning: Resultar al final / Acudir público a un evento / Apagar luces
examples: Despite our early logistical worries, the conference turned out wonderfully.
It turned out that the anonymous whistleblower was the chief accountant.
Thousands of devoted citizens turned out to welcome the returning athletes.
Make sure you turn out the lights and lock the front door before leaving.
Things rarely turn out exactly as planned, but adaptability ensures survival.

meaning: Aparecer de improviso / Subir el volumen o calefacción / Encontrarse algo perdido
examples: He turned up at our doorstep at midnight without calling in advance.
Could you turn up the central heating? It feels freezing in this room.
Don't worry about your lost passport; it will surely turn up somewhere.
Turn up the radio! This is my favorite classical guitar concerto.
Fresh forensic clues turned up during the second sweep of the crime scene.

meaning: Darse cuenta por fin de una realidad o peligro inminente
examples: Governments must wake up to the acute realities of climate volatility.
He finally woke up to the fact that his lifestyle was ruining his health.
Society needs to wake up to the psychological dangers of teenage screen addiction.
She woke up to the realization that her job offered zero intellectual growth.
It took a catastrophic financial audit for the board to wake up to corporate waste.

meaning: Desgastar algo por el uso / Agotar físicamente a una persona
examples: Running on concrete pavements will wear out your running shoes quickly.
Taking care of four energetic toddlers all day will completely wear you out.
The brake pads on your car have worn out and must be replaced immediately.
Don't wear yourself out trying to please people who never show gratitude.
His repetitive, bitter complaints eventually wore out his friends' patience.

meaning: Terminar en un lugar o situación / Liquidar una empresa / Tomar el pelo a alguien
examples: If you drive without a valid license, you will wind up in serious legal trouble.
The court ordered the bankrupt corporation to wind up its commercial affairs.
Don't get upset by his sarcastic remarks; he is just trying to wind you up.
Let's wind up our meeting by summarizing the actionable steps for Monday.
He wound up working in an art restoration laboratory after studying chemistry.

meaning: Hacer ejercicio / Salir bien las cosas / Calcular o resolver un dilema
examples: She works out at the fitness center four times a week to stay healthy.
Don't worry excessively about the future; things usually work out in the end.
Our financial accountants worked out the exact tax liability for this quarter.
I cannot work out why this mechanical watch suddenly stopped ticking.
The peace negotiations worked out better than anyone dared to anticipate.
